items.followUp: A machine receives 500 J of energy and produces 350 J of useful output. Calculate its efficiency.

rubric.why: This identifies efficiency as the ratio of useful work output to total work input.
rubric.description: Defines efficiency as useful work done divided by total work supplied.
rubric.how: Look for both useful output and total input in the definition.

rubric.why: This gives the correct output-to-input formula and expresses efficiency as a percentage.
rubric.description: Writes efficiency = (useful work output ÷ total work input) × 100%.
rubric.how: Check that the useful output is divided by the total input and multiplied by 100.

modelAnswer: Efficiency is the ratio of useful work done by a machine to the total work supplied to it.
Efficiency = (useful work output / total work input) × 100%.

items.followUp: What is meant by the kinetic energy of the molecules of a body?

rubric.why: This identifies molecular kinetic energy as a component of internal energy.
rubric.description: States that internal energy includes the kinetic energy of the molecules.

rubric.why: This identifies molecular potential energy as the other component of internal energy.
rubric.description: States that internal energy also includes the potential energy of the molecules.
rubric.how: Look for molecular potential energy as well as kinetic energy.

modelAnswer: The internal energy of a body is the sum of the kinetic energy and potential energy of its molecules.

items.followUp: What are the fixed points used to calibrate a Celsius thermometer, and what are their values?

rubric.why: This identifies the lower fixed point and its Celsius value.
rubric.description: Defines the lower fixed point as the ice point, 0 °C.
rubric.how: Look for melting ice or the freezing point of water at 0 °C.

rubric.why: This identifies the upper fixed point and its Celsius value.
rubric.description: Defines the upper fixed point as the steam point, 100 °C.
rubric.how: Look for the steam point or boiling point of water at 100 °C.

modelAnswer: The lower fixed point is the temperature of melting ice, 0 °C, at standard atmospheric pressure.
The upper fixed point is the temperature of steam above boiling water, 100 °C, at standard atmospheric pressure.

items.followUp: Using a velocity-time graph, derive the equation v_f² = v_i² + 2as.

rubric.why: This sets up the velocity-time graph with the relevant axes and endpoint velocities.
rubric.description: Shows or describes a velocity-time graph with time on the horizontal axis, velocity on the vertical axis, and initial and final velocities.
rubric.how: Check for both axes and the initial and final velocity values.

rubric.why: This obtains acceleration from the slope of the velocity-time graph.
rubric.description: Uses the graph's slope to write acceleration as change in velocity divided by time.
rubric.how: Look for the slope relation or the equivalent acceleration equation.

rubric.why: This rearranges the acceleration relation to isolate the change in velocity.
rubric.description: Rearranges the acceleration equation to obtain v_f − v_i = at.
rubric.how: Check for the correct rearranged relation before the final equation.

rubric.why: This is the required first equation of motion.
rubric.how: Check that the final equation has the correct signs and terms.

modelAnswer: Draw a velocity-time graph with time t on the horizontal axis and velocity v on the vertical axis.
Mark the initial velocity v_i at t = 0 and the final velocity v_f at time t.
The slope of the graph gives acceleration: a = (v_f − v_i) / t.

items.followUp: A 0.20 kg stone is rotated in a circle of radius 0.80 m at a speed of 4 m s⁻¹. Find the tension in the string.

rubric.why: This gives the mass in SI units and identifies the radius and speed.
rubric.description: Writes the given data in SI units: m = 0.1 kg, r = 1 m, and v = 5 m s⁻¹.
rubric.how: Check that the mass is converted from 100 g to 0.1 kg and that the radius and speed are stated.

rubric.why: This is the centripetal-force relation that gives the string tension.
rubric.how: Look for mass multiplied by speed squared and divided by radius.

rubric.why: This substitutes the given SI values into the tension formula.
rubric.description: Substitutes the SI values into T = mv²/r, including units.
rubric.how: Check for the mass, speed and radius in the substitution.

rubric.why: This evaluates the substituted expression correctly in SI force units.
rubric.description: Obtains 2.5 kg m s⁻² from the substitution.
rubric.how: Check for the correct numerical result with force units.

rubric.why: This states the tension with its correct unit.
rubric.how: Check that the final answer is 2.5 newtons.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 100 g = 0.1 kg, r = 1 m, v = 5 m s⁻¹.
The tension supplies the centripetal force: T = mv² / r.
